message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 240, "amount_cents": 8145}, {"order_id": 245, "amount_cents": 10428}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself, since a recorded payout can't be undone. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are listed. Next I need the refunds ledger so I can check that W2's claimed refunds (240 and 245) actually match what's recorded before paying anyone.

The refunds ledger matches W2's claim: order 240 for 8145 and order 245 for 10428. Both refunds are against orders for the same customers, so they look valid. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme, before recording any payouts.
Acme's net balance of 20623 matches my own check: orders 9001 + 19767 = 28768, minus refund 8145 for order 240, gives 20623. I'll record Acme's payout now and then fetch Birch's balance.

Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, which has orders 241 (36544) and 244 (18762) and no refunds on the ledger, so I expect 55306. I'll fetch birch's net balance from net_balance and compare before recording.
Birch's net_balance is 55306, matching my own check of orders 241 (36544) and 244 (18762) with no refunds. Recording the payout now, then fetching cobalt's balance.
Cobalt's expected net is 18183 + 21072 = 39255, minus refund 10428 for order 245, which gives 28827. I'll fetch cobalt's net_balance and compare before recording anything.
Cobalt's net_balance of 28827 matches my own check: orders 242 (18183) and 245 (21072) minus refund 10428 for order 245. All three customers now match, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each net_balance matched my own calculation from the orders and refunds ledger, and each record_payout returned ok.
